title: A lean redesign of the morning sedation interruption process in an intensive care unit: an improvement report
abstract: Problem: in a 16-bed intensive care unit, sedation was interrupted on 38 percent of eligible patient-days although the safety screen was documented on 71 percent. Intervention: value stream mapping and A3 cycles testing removal of an informal approval step and a shared time with respiratory therapy. Measures: weekly completed interruptions, paired breathing trials, self-extubation and rescue boluses. Results and conclusions will be written after April 2027.
introduction: The benefits of daily sedation interruption depend on adherence, which is much lower in routine practice than in trials. In the retrieved records, the process fails after the screen, at waits for authority and hand-offs.
methods: Eight-week baseline, value stream mapping with gemba walks, A3 cycles with two countermeasures in sequence, daily tally by the charge nurse, run charts with pre-specified rules and a days-between-events chart for self-extubation; SQUIRE 2.0 reporting.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present the value stream map, the run charts with countermeasure dates and the safety charts.
discussion: The discussion will interpret any shift against the run chart rules, compare the countermeasures with those in the retrieved reports and state what the unit keeps.
limitations: One unit; before-after design; possible documentation drift.
conclusion: To be written after April 2027; it will be limited to this unit's process measures and will not claim an effect on ventilator days.
summary: SQUIRE-structured draft with results left empty until data exist.
